items.problem: The release overflow setting does not reach the sim's code where the sim actually runs. The per-package override ([profile.release.package.sim] and .protocol, the mechanism ADR 0002 part 4 names) only covers code that rustc generates inside sim's and protocol's own compilation. sim's small, #[inline] and generic functions are generated in the crate that calls them (room, client-endpoint, sim-wasm, devtools, and later server and navbake). Those crates have overflow checks off in release, so there the checks vanish and the code wraps silently. Two statements therefore do not hold in the release server or the release Wasm: the comment on line 21 ('Overflow checks in every profile for the simulation and the protocol') and ADR part 4's 'a debug client and a release server never disagree on overflow'. E1, M5 and K1b hold as worded, since the flag does reach sim's and protocol's own compilation. But no test inside the sim package can see this, nor can PM-0002-53's planned 'committed test in sim'. This is not OVERFLOW-WASM, which treats native release as proven; native release has the same hole. Nor is it OVERFLOW-PER-CRATE, which covers crates that hold sim arithmetic; this is sim's own code compiled into crates that hold none, so that remedy does not close it. Reach is zero today. It starts with the first sim function called from another crate, which is what Fable builds next.
items.evidence: Reproduce with /home/user/Shamble-Frontlines/.gate/foundation-toolchain-wt/.checkpoints/foundation-toolchain/rust-reviewer-overflow-xcrate.sh (re-run into /home/user/Shamble-Frontlines/.gate/rust-reviewer-r1-repro). In a scratch copy, sim gets add_plain (no attribute), add_inline (#[inline]), add_generic<T>, Tick::next (#[inline], u32 + 1) and add_never (#[inline(never)]). room depends on sim and calls each with black_box(MAX) and 1 under #[should_panic(expected = "attempt to add with overflow")]. Test profile: 5 of 5 panic. cargo test --release -p room: 4 FAILED ('test did not panic as expected'); only add_never panics. The -v output after a clean shows 'crate-name sim --crate-type lib opt-level=3 -C overflow-checks=on' and 'crate-name room --crate-type lib opt-level=3', with no overflow flag. An integration test inside the sim package (crates/sim/tests/) passes, because package overrides cover all of sim's targets. Wasm32 release, with a scratch sim-wasm cdylib exporting step(a,b): calling sim::add_plain gives a 329-byte .wasm with no 'attempt to add with overflow' string; calling add_never gives 20,353 bytes with the panic present (raw sizes of a toy export). The mechanism in rustc 1.99.1: compiler/rustc_codegen_ssa/src/mir/block.rs:747-753, 'if !bx.sess().overflow_checks() && msg.is_optional_overflow_check() { const_cond = Some(expected); }', so the setting of the crate doing code generation wins. And compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/cross_crate_inline.rs:117-118, 'Assert terminators are similar to calls ... so those are just treated as statements', so small checked functions become inlinable across crates in optimized builds. The Cargo book (1.99.1, profiles, 'Overrides and generics') says the same for opt-level: 'the code may be generated in the crate where it is instantiated, and thus may use the optimization settings of that crate'. ADR 0002:1319 (PM-0002-53): 'a committed test in sim run in the four builds'.

items.problem: The Risks bullet rightly says the cut "is not a sandbox", but it leaves "the rest" to this review, and the plan that held the detail (section 4.4, which also understates it as "close the two easy ways out (docker, sudo)") is deleted before ready. The rest: code inside the cut keeps the runner's uid and shares the filesystem and process table with what runs after it, so it can get code run outside the cut. Exploit sketch: a compromised dev dependency (vitest, vite, or the rolldown and lightningcss native binaries, all of which run inside the cut) writes `core.fsmonitor = <script>` into the workspace's .git/config. After the cut, actions/checkout's post-job step runs `git submodule foreach --recursive ...` outside the cut, and git runs the script there with the network, the docker group and passwordless sudo.
items.evidence: toolchain.yml:68-73 (setpriv keeps uid 1001; no mount or PID namespace). CI log, PR job 131510257155, lines 447-463: checkout's post step runs `/usr/bin/git submodule foreach --recursive ...` after the cut. Local test in a fresh scratch repository: a hook planted in `core.fsmonitor`, then `git submodule status` (the same submodule-listing code path; the guard refused the exact `foreach` here) ran the hook (marker lines with args 2 and 1). git-config(1): core.fsmonitor holds "the pathname of the \"fsmonitor\" hook command". network_namespaces(7) isolates only "the UNIX domain abstract socket namespace", so pathname sockets stay reachable: the D-Bus system bus, and systemd-resolved's socket if the image has it, through which name lookups leave the machine (from documentation, untested on the runner). Code inside can also signal the runner's own processes, which run as the same user. Impact: contents: read and no secrets today. Possible reach into main-scope caches, including the Playwright cache that the required smoke check restores, rests on recall (JavaScript actions carry the cache token). gate.yml's toolkit dependencies have the same exposure today.

items.problem: setpriv drops privileges without `--inh-caps=-all` (setpriv(1)'s own advice when dropping from root) and without `--bounding-set=-all`. The cut prints `id` and `ip -o link` but asserts none of its properties. Today the result is right, but it relies on sudo's root having empty inheritable and ambient sets, and on the step shell not being root. Exploit sketch: none on today's runner. If the step shell ran as root (a container job, or a self-hosted runner), `--reuid="$(id -u)"` becomes 0, so the code inside the cut keeps root and full capabilities (and could re-enter the host network namespace) while every step stays green.
items.evidence: toolchain.yml:69-74; the CI log prints `uid=1001(runner) gid=65534(nogroup)` and only `lo` (PR job 131510257155 :254-255), printed but never checked. setpriv(1): "Setting a uid or gid does not change capabilities, although the exec call at the end might change capabilities. This means that, if you are root, you probably want to do something like: setpriv --reuid=1000 --regid=1000 --inh-caps=-all". Local test, util-linux 2.39.3 as root: with the job's flags, CapInh/CapPrm/CapEff/CapAmb 0, CapBnd = the parent's 000001fffeffffff, NoNewPrivs 1; with `--inh-caps=-all --bounding-set=-all` added, the same but CapBnd 0000000000000000, exit 0. The full bounding set is inert today: under no_new_privs "the set-user-ID and set-group-ID bits as well as file capabilities will be disabled" (setpriv(1)).

items.problem: On the pinned 1.99.1, a member's 'default-features' setting now overrides the [workspace.dependencies] entry in edition 2024; from 1.85 to 1.98 the same combination was an error. Separately, one cargo command unifies features across all the members it builds. So ADR 0002 part 3's 'the maths-relevant features of the dependencies it shares with server are set once in [workspace.dependencies]' (:212-217) is not enforced by Cargo. A member can quietly set its own default-features, and the gate's planned feature comparison only notices that after the fact. This starts with the first third-party maths crate.
items.evidence: Edition guide (doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2024/cargo-inherited-default-features.html): 'Starting with Rust 1.99, default-features on an inherited dependency in a 2024 Edition package overrides the value from [workspace.dependencies]' and 'The original 2024 Edition behavior in Rust 1.85 through 1.98 rejected this combination'. Offline repro: a path crate depx with default = ["std"] is listed in [workspace.dependencies], and sim takes '{ workspace = true, default-features = false }'. On 1.99.1 there is no error or warning, and 'cargo tree -e features -p sim' shows depx with no features. Once room takes '{ workspace = true }', 'cargo tree -e features -p sim -p room' shows depx with features 'default' and 'std' for both.
